report:
Finding: Model B carries a strong start-of-sequence “headline/caption/news” style prior relative to Model A.

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Where the signal is: The difference is overwhelmingly anchored at position 0 and remains large through the first few tokens, peaking late (layer 25 p0 = 322). This looks like a global BOS/start-of-sequence style shift rather than a narrow skill.
- Logit-lens content:
  - Repeated headline/caption adjectives at positions 2–4 across many late layers: “iconic,” “tragic,” “tragedy,” “vivid,” “timeless,” “colorful,” “loud,” “vibrant,” “furry,” plus event nouns like “hurricane,” “refugees,” “victims.” This cluster is characteristic of news, culture, and photo-caption language.
  - Proper-noun/Title-Case and headline markers around pos1: “Driver,” “Names,” “Sessions,” “headlines,” “headlights,” “van,” “Vincent,” “Hunter,” etc., suggesting capitalized entities and headline formatting.
  - Start-of-sequence verbs/imperatives at pos0 in mid/late layers: “try,” “optimize,” “strive,” “refused,” “blitz,” “worst,” “adhere,” “check,” “prepare,” which fit newsy/clickbait or guide-style openings.
  - List/Title patterns: numerals as top tokens at L13 pos1 (6, 8, 7, 9, 5) and frequent “All/all,” consistent with listicles or headline scaffolding.
- What it is not: There’s no strong signature of code, math, safety RLHF boilerplate, or a specific technical domain.

Interpretation: Model B appears more biased toward producing news/culture headlines or caption-like, sensational/adjectival prose at the very start of sequences. I can’t name a specific training objective, but the consistent lexical field and capitalization patterns suggest additional exposure/fine-tuning on news, entertainment, or caption/title data, yielding a BOS-anchored stylistic prior.
